claim: A substantial strand in the formation of the Sri Lankan Malay community came from coercive mobility within the Dutch and later British imperial systems: from the late seventeenth century the VOC used Ceylon as a place of banishment for political opponents and royal lineages from the Indonesian archipelago, while soldiers, convicts, enslaved people and their entourages also moved to the island; British rule added further Malay military migration.
bounded_by: The later Sri Lankan Malay community had heterogeneous origins and identity formation was gradual. Not every migrant from the archipelago was Muslim, an exile, or a voluntary migrant.
notes: Strong side-story candidate: Ceylon as an imperial exile node linking Java, Sulawesi, the Malay world and South Africa.
